commits.author: Claude
commits.subject: Leave panes the repository has no files for off the report
commits.body:
A report on a repository with no migrations said its migrations pane did
not apply, one with no API spec said the same of the contract, and a change
with no Go file was told no coverage profile was found. None of that tells
the reader anything, and it buries the one line that matters: a pane that
did apply and could not run.

Run now asks each pane with nothing in the change whether it has anything
in the whole tree. A pane with no files anywhere is recorded as
not-applicable, a new substrate state findings.json keeps and no renderer
mentions. A pane the repository has that this change did not reach stays
skipped and is still listed, folded away, so "not touched" and "not
checked" remain distinguishable. Coverage gains a coverableFiles count;
when it is zero the markdown, the page, the sidebar, and the posted
evidence table leave coverage out. The page's interface section now
renders only when the change touches UI, for the same reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BX9m5Bv1AXr9d9N34uACjm

+with its state (`ran`, `skipped`, `failed`, `not-applicable`) so an agent
+reading it knows which panes exist.

diff --git a/internal/run/run.go b/internal/run/run.go
--- a/internal/run/run.go
+++ b/internal/run/run.go
@@ -110,0 +111,32 @@
+	// Every path in the tree under review, listed once and only if a pane
+	// turns out to have nothing in the change to look at. It answers a
+	// different question from scope: not "does this pane apply to the change"
+	// but "does this pane apply to the repository". A repository with no
+	// migrations gets no mention of migrations; one whose migrations this
+	// change did not touch is told so, quietly.
+	var allPaths []string
+	listAll := func() []string {
+		if allPaths != nil {
+			return allPaths
+		}
+		var blobs map[string]string
+		var lerr error
+		if tgt.Head == "" {
+			blobs, lerr = repo.WorktreeBlobs()
+		} else {
+			blobs, lerr = repo.Blobs(tgt.Head)
+		}
+		if lerr != nil {
+			// Unknown whether the pane applies: fall back to saying it was
+			// skipped, the state that still gets a line on the report.
+			allPaths = []string{}
+			return allPaths
+		}
+		allPaths = make([]string, 0, len(blobs))
+		for path := range blobs {
+			allPaths = append(allPaths, path)
+		}
+		sort.Strings(allPaths)
+		return allPaths
+	}

+// A pane the repository has no files for gets no row: the table accounts for
+// the checks that could have run, and "no linter is configured" is not one.
+// The same for coverage on a change with nothing a profile could cover.
+func TestBuildBodyOmitsWhatDoesNotApply(t *testing.T) {
+	rep := sampleReport()
+	if p := Build(rep, prTarget(), "", nil); strings.Contains(p.Body, "| lint |") {
+		t.Fatalf("a not-applicable pane must not get a row:\n%s", p.Body)
+	}
+	rep.Coverage.CoverableFiles = 0
+	if p := Build(rep, prTarget(), "", nil); strings.Contains(p.Body, "diff coverage") {
+		t.Fatalf("coverage must not be mentioned when no changed file is coverable:\n%s", p.Body)
+	}
+}

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    feat: post a session's findings as one GitHub PR review
    
    Add `redline post --pr N`, the one command that writes to GitHub. It loads
    the session `review` recorded and submits its findings as a single pull
    request review (event COMMENT — it reports, never requests changes or
    approves). Findings with file:line become line-anchored comments; the rest,
    and a coverage preamble stating what was and was not checked, go in the
    review body. The preamble is read off the report's own substrate and
    coverage records, so it can never claim a check ran that did not — the part
    a bare Copilot comment never provides.
    
    Posting is explicit and never a side effect: run, review, and ingest stay
    read-only. It refuses unless the loaded session is the PR named. It is
    idempotent per (PR, head SHA): each comment carries a hidden hex-encoded
    fingerprint marker, so a re-post drops comments already present and a re-run
    with no new findings on an already-reviewed commit posts nothing.
    
    The payload logic lives in internal/post as pure functions (unit-tested
    without a token); cmd/redline/post.go does the gh I/O. gh supplies the
    credentials; Redline never handles one. --report-url links the full report
    from the body; --dry-run prints the payload instead of posting.
    
    Also correct the now-stale "never posts to GitHub" language in the README,
    the command doc, and the design doc to match the reversed decision.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    feat: post a session's findings as one GitHub PR review
    
    Add `redline post --pr N`, the one command that writes to GitHub. It loads
    the session `review` recorded and submits its findings as a single pull
    request review (event COMMENT — it reports, never requests changes or
    approves). Findings with file:line become line-anchored comments; the rest,
    and a coverage preamble stating what was and was not checked, go in the
    review body. The preamble is read off the report's own substrate and
    coverage records, so it can never claim a check ran that did not — the part
    a bare Copilot comment never provides.
    
    Posting is explicit and never a side effect: run, review, and ingest stay
    read-only. It refuses unless the loaded session is the PR named. It is
    idempotent per (PR, head SHA): each comment carries a hidden hex-encoded
    fingerprint marker, so a re-post drops comments already present and a re-run
    with no new findings on an already-reviewed commit posts nothing.
    
    The payload logic lives in internal/post as pure functions (unit-tested
    without a token); cmd/redline/post.go does the gh I/O. gh supplies the
    credentials; Redline never handles one. --report-url links the full report
    from the body; --dry-run prints the payload instead of posting.
    
    Also correct the now-stale "never posts to GitHub" language in the README,
    the command doc, and the design doc to match the reversed decision.

envelopes.promptFragment:
Reviewing Go.

Errors are values and the wrapping chain is the contract. A function that adds
context to an error wraps it with %w when a caller may need errors.Is or
errors.As to match it, and formats with %v when the chain should stop there.
An error is handled once: code that logs it and returns it has handled it
twice, and the caller reports it again. A dropped error is a finding unless the
code says why.

context.Context is the first parameter, named ctx, and travels down every call
that can block. Look for a function that takes one and ignores it, for
context.Background() created deep inside a request path, and for a context
kept in a struct field. Cancellation only works when the value carrying it
reaches the blocking call.

Every goroutine needs a defined end. Ask what stops it and what happens when
the caller returns first. A goroutine started per request with no cancellation
is a leak. A WaitGroup whose Add runs inside the goroutine is a race. Anything
a closure captures and two goroutines write needs a mutex or a channel.

Nil is legal for slices, maps, channels, function values, pointers, and
interfaces, and it behaves differently for each. Reading a nil map works and
writing one panics. A nil pointer inside a non-nil interface compares unequal
to nil, which is how a returned error becomes non-nil by accident.

Interfaces belong to the consumer. A new interface declared beside its only
implementation usually belongs in the package that calls it. Satisfaction is
checked at compile time, so a method added only to satisfy an interface is
either used or dead.

Tests are table-driven by convention: a slice of named cases with a subtest per
case under t.Run. Look for state shared between cases, for t.Parallel over a
captured loop variable, and for assertions on error strings where errors.Is
says what was meant.

Load-bearing idioms: defer for cleanup that must run on every path, a zero
value that is usable without construction, and early returns over nesting.
